item.title: AI Is Smarter Than Ever. So Where’s the Revolution? | Plain English
item.itunes:author: Plain English with Derek Thompson
item.description:
00:00:00 Der allwissende Tutor: Warum KI-Schüler schlechter abschneiden 00:04:00 Intro, Werbung und Begrüßung von Ethan Mollick 00:05:30 Warum selbst Top-Prognostiker den KI-Fortschritt unterschätzen 00:07:00 Warum KI noch nicht in der Produktivität ankommt 00:09:30 O-Ringe und Mülleimer: Warum Firmen sich so schwer umbauen 00:12:00 Interne, öffentliche und Alltagsmodelle: Dreimal „KI“ 00:15:00 Paradox Expertise: Profis profitieren, Einsteiger verlieren 00:18:00 KI an der Uni: Verbieten oder lehren? 00:23:00 Prompting ist tot – Schreiben bleibt Handarbeit 00:26:00 Denken als Fitnessstudio: Wann die Mühe der Sinn ist 00:28:00 Wissen ohne Verständnis: KI löst Mathe-Probleme 00:33:00 Was von Wissenschaft und Forschung wertvoll bleibt 00:36:00 Nachrufe und Hochzeitsreden: Wann menschliche Arbeit zählt 00:41:00 Geschmack, Urteilskraft und verschwimmende Berufe 00:44:00 Warum gutes Präsentieren wichtiger wird 00:47:30 Die Neuheit: Persönliche Agenten wie Muse 00:53:00 Millionen Agenten gegen den Kundenservice 00:57:00 Agenten-Schwärme: Was Mollick falsch eingeschätzt hat 01:00:00 Wandel auch ohne bessere KI 01:01:00 „Nicht AGI-pilled genug“: Ausblick und Koexistenz
AI can analyze anything, write anything, solve almost any puzzle. But struggle strengthens our brains and sharpens our minds ... and removing it entirely may come with a dire cost.
Derek Thompson explores the paradoxes of AI with Ethan Mollick, whose new book, 'Co-Existence,' examines how AI is changing the way we learn and work. They discuss how AI makes experts more powerful while automating the junior work that creates them in the first place, why students perform better via AI but learn less, and whether some friction may actually be worth preserving.
If you have questions, observations, or ideas for future episodes, email us at PlainEnglish@Spotify.com.
Host: Derek Thompson Guest: Ethan Mollick Producer: Devon Baroldi Additional Production Support: Ben Glicksman

Regulierung und Zusammenarbeit 01:15:00 Haben wir KI noch unter Kontrolle? 01:17:00 Publikumsfragen: Schulden und was Kinder studieren sollten
What could the next few years of AI progress mean for the economy and daily life?
In this year’s Per Jacobsson Foundation Lecture, Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark will examine the potential implications of faster scientific discovery, advances in robotics, machine-driven businesses, and AI systems that may contribute to their own development.
The event will be opened by IMF Deputy Managing Director Nigel Clarke and moderated by Raghuram Rajan, Chair of the Per Jacobsson Foundation, with Yan Shen, Professor of Economics at Peking University, and V. Anantha Nageswaran, Chief Economic Adviser to the Government of India, as discussants.

Dwarkesh Patel is one of the most important voices in the artificial intelligence world. Deeply embedded in San Francisco’s tech community, he has interviewed nearly every tech chief executive at length.
This week’s guest host, Tyler Cowen, a professor of economics at George Mason University, sits down with Mr. Patel to discuss why researchers are resigning, whether A.I. could become conscious and if he’ll ever get an A.I. girlfriend.
